item.title: Middle East live: Israel urges residents of Lebanon's Nabatieh to leave ahead of possible strikes
item.description: Israeli forces on Tuesday warned residents of the southern Lebanese city of Nabatieh to immediately evacuate ahead of expected strikes. The warning comes a day after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered his military to intensify attacks on Hezbollah to "crush" the Tehran-backed group. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.

item.title: Israel pounds Lebanon with fresh air strikes, vows to 'crush' Hezbollah
item.description: Israel intensified air strikes across southern and eastern Lebanon on Monday after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to “crush” Hezbollah, deepening fears of a wider regional conflict. The escalation comes despite an April ceasefire and as another round of US-Iran talks takes place in Doha in a bid to negotiate terms for a broader Middle East peace deal.

item.title: Possible Iran-US deal: What we know about the key issues on both sides
item.description: The United States and Iran have downplayed prospects for a rapid deal to end the Middle East war, despite signs of progress in talks. Key sticking points remain over Iran’s nuclear programme, control of the Strait of Hormuz, sanctions relief and a possible ceasefire in Lebanon, with both sides signalling that major issues are still unresolved.

item.title: Palestine's Eid dampened by consequences of war on livestock
item.description: Palestinians in Gaza facing another grim Eid holiday, which starts Tuesday evening. The livestock sector there has been destroyed by the war, and Israel isn't allowing the import of live animals, making the traditional animal sacrifice nearly impossible. Restrictions on border crossings also mean Palestinians are unable to perform the pilgrimage to Mecca.

item.title: Israel Steps Up Lebanon Offensive as U.S. Pushes for Iran Peace Deal
item.description: Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militant group, has also kept up rocket and drone attacks on Israeli troops, as the escalation threatens to complicate diplomatic efforts.

item.title: Israeli opposition leader Lapid says Trump’s emerging deal with Iran is `bad for the region’
item.description: Israel's opposition leader Yair Lapid says the U.S.-Iran deal fails to meet Israel's goals and is criticizing Prime Minister Netanyahu for allowing Washington to negotiate with little Israeli input

item.title: Israel strikes Lebanese village and calls up more troops in the region
item.description: The Israeli army has issued a fresh set of evacuation orders for 10 villages in Southern Lebanon as it prepares for a new round of military strikes. Israel and the militant group Hezbollah have been trading deadly fire despite a ceasefire. In fact, two far-right Israeli ministers are calling for more severe military action in Lebanon, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered an escalation of the offensive against Hezbollah.

item.title: Netanyahu says Israel will intensify strikes against Hezbollah
item.description: The Israeli military hits targets in eastern Lebanon after the prime minister announces further strikes.

item.title: Fresh strikes test fragile Israel-Hezbollah truce
item.description: Israeli strikes killed two people in southern Lebanon during the weekend despite the ongoing ceasefire with Hezbollah. At the same time, Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem rejected talks with Israel, opposed disarmament, and called for protests against the Lebanese government, drawing condemnation from the United States.

item.title: Nuclear issue remains key obstacle in Iran-US deal
item.description: Simon Mabon, Professor of International Politics and Middle East Studies at Lancaster University, joins FRANCE 24 to discuss the latest developments in the Middle East. While Iran and the United States are still exploring a possible deal to end the conflict, both sides are now downplaying hopes of an imminent breakthrough after appearing close to an agreement just days ago.
